description: KNOWN-BAD question set — the navigation eval's negative control. Every question here asks a correct, answerable navigation question against bad-fixture-vault, and every one MUST fail, each for a single distinct seeded reason. A run of this set that is not 0/7 means the instrument has stopped being able to detect that class of defect: the fixture is the known-bad input the gate rule requires before a green from questions.json is trusted. `must_fail_because` names the defect; `note_contains` is the substring the runner's failure note must carry, so the control asserts WHICH check tripped rather than merely that something failed.
label: known-bad

questions.topic: off-vault edge target: which in-vault service does the Context Service call?
questions.must_fail_because: the edge's target is [[Partner Gateway]], which is not a page in this vault, so the store reports external_target: true and no in-vault target resolves

questions.topic: unresolved template endpoint: what endpoint does the Reporting Job call on the Frontend?
questions.must_fail_because: the served endpoint is /api/{tenant}/export — an unresolved {template}, a shape rather than an address

questions.topic: condition-less http-call: under what condition does the Frontend call the Backend?
questions.must_fail_because: the http-call edge carries no condition: key at all, so the 'under what condition' half of the question has no served answer

questions.topic: self-confirming substring: is the `roles` collection in the Scheduler's shared-store coupling?
questions.must_fail_because: the collection list states accessroles,aclentries,agents,groups,users and NOT roles — a containment test against the stdout blob stays GREEN because `accessroles` contains the substring `roles`; only token-exact endpoint matching fails here

questions.topic: stale provenance: at which source line does the Audit Sink's store coupling live?
questions.must_fail_because: the edge still points at sink.py:9, the line the call used to occupy — a provenance pointer that no longer resolves cannot be verified against code

questions.topic: hop bar exceeded (query): does the Edge Relay reach the Frontend within 3 hops?
questions.must_fail_because: the Frontend sits 4 hops from the Edge Relay. Issued at --depth max_hops the target is simply absent and gets mis-reported as unreachable; probing to max_hops+2 finds it at hop 4 and fails it against the declared bar of 3

questions.topic: hop bar exceeded (bridge): shortest path from the Edge Relay to the Frontend
questions.must_fail_because: the store's own BFS returns a 4-link path (Edge Relay -> Tier One -> Tier Two -> Tier Three -> Frontend) against a declared bar of 3

questions.topic: dynamic distinguishability: is the Bad Report Gateway's dynamic family distinguishable from a resolved call?
questions.must_fail_because: a second edge is typed `dynamic` while stating no unresolved expression at all, so nothing downstream can tell which call site could not be resolved or act on it — the family is present but not distinguishable

questions.topic: physical subscribes-to provenance: which declaration creates the Bad Report Queue subscription?
questions.must_fail_because: the subscribes-to edge names a target and a type and carries no provenance at all, so nothing ties it to a declaration file a reader could open

questions.topic: freshness: which commit was the Bad Report Gateway's dynamic edge extracted from?
questions.must_fail_because: extracted_from.sha is the literal string 'unknown', so the record cannot be tied to a commit and its staleness is unknowable

questions.topic: freshness completeness: when was the Bad Report Gateway's invokes edge extracted?
questions.must_fail_because: the invokes edge's extracted_from omits `at`. Measured consequence: the STORE drops the whole incomplete object rather than serving a partial one, so the served edge carries no extracted_from at all

questions.topic: co-writer lookup: which collections does the Bad Report Gateway share with the Frontend?
questions.must_fail_because: the flat `endpoint` string still advertises mongo:reports,report_runs while the structured `collections` list a consumer actually reads carries only `reports` — the same self-confirming shape as the deleted `,roles`, one level up

questions.topic: blast radius: does the Bad Report Gateway WRITE the collections it shares with the Frontend?
questions.must_fail_because: access.this claims read-only while the edge is a writer in reality, so a blast-radius question returns the wrong answer with full confidence
